about: The vocabulary of recipe checks. A check is { kind, says, ...the fields its kind row names }. Adding a check kind is adding a row here: the validator reads every rule from the row. Field shapes: path = a list of keys starting at one of the roots (and reading only earlier steps), words = a non-empty list of non-empty strings, count = a whole number above 0, catalog = one of the catalogs, list = any list.

roots.meaning: The output of the step the check belongs to.
The input the person gave the workflow.
The output of an earlier step; the key after it is that step's id.

catalogs.meaning: A workflow recipe the account can run.
A row in one of the account's lists.
A record in the account's data.

kinds.meaning: Every value at path is also a value at of.
The values at path include every value at of, or every value listed in values.
Every value at path appears in the text at in.
The text at path contains none of the listed words.

fields.refusal: must list the words to keep out.

kinds.meaning: The values at path hold at least count different values.

fields.refusal: must be a whole number above 0.

kinds.meaning: Every id at path names something that exists in the catalog.
